correctness.rationale: For a genuine centrally symmetric convex hexagon, center origin and label six ccw vertices v1,v2,v3,-v1,-v2,-v3. Strict convexity and genuine vertices yield a=det(v1,v2)>0, b=det(v2,v3)>0, c=det(v1,v3)>0, with area S=a+b+c. The published Horvath--Langi identity c_tr=1+8 max_{x in boundary} A_K(x)/S uses A_K(x)=1/2 max_{y in K} det(x,y). Since max_y det(x,y) is convex in x, its maximum over K occurs at a vertex, and boundary vertices suffice. At v1,v2,v3 the A-values are respectively max(a,c)/2, max(a,b)/2, max(b,c)/2, and opposite vertices give same values. Thus EXACTLY max A=M/2 and c_tr(K)=1+4M/S; AM-max gives M>=S/3, hence 7/3. Equality iff a=b=c; the determinant normalization v1=(1,0),v3=(0,1) then gives v2=(1,1), namely an affine-regular hexagon. Conversely the affine-regular model has S=3,M=1 and ratio 7/3. This is a valid unrestricted analytic proof, not a finite experiment; the source package references the published planar formula as its sole nonstandard input. Separately checked exact rational examples but did not infer universal truth from them.

originality.rationale: A 2008 theorem of Gronchi and Longinetti, independently described in a detailed mathematical review, says that the normalized smallest vertex-ear triangle functional F(P)=min_j area(conv{z_(j-1),z_j,z_(j+1)})/area(P) on convex n-gons is maximized precisely by affine-regular n-gons. This is a stronger earlier theorem that mathematically implies BOTH submitted conclusions when n=6 and P is centrally symmetric. With cyclic vertices v1,v2,v3,-v1,-v2,-v3 and a=det(v1,v2), b=det(v2,v3), c=det(v1,v3), S=a+b+c, M=max{a,b,c}, the six consecutive-vertex ear areas are (S-2a)/2, (S-2b)/2, (S-2c)/2, repeated in opposite pairs; hence F(P)=1/2-M/S. The published Horvath--Langi support-triangle identity plus extremality of a convex support function at vertices gives c^tr(P)=1+4M/S=3-4F(P). The 2008 sharp maximization F(P)<=F(regular_6)=1/6 therefore yields c^tr(P)>=7/3, and its unique affine-regular equality class yields exactly the submitted equality clause. This is implication-level complete coverage, not just similarity of titles, numerical constants or proof methods. The Gronchi--Longinetti full primary PDF was not accessible (author repository access closed and public mirror 403); the exact functional and maximal-equality theorem are explicitly recorded in a published mathematical abstract/review, enough to establish this decisive mathematical implication. No claim of having read that inaccessible full text is made.

value.rationale: The restricted symmetric-hexagon minimization and equality classification are intrinsically natural geometric questions, but the submitted result adds no independently unknown exact fact beyond Gronchi--Longinetti (2008) once the two standard area quantities are related. The normalized minimum consecutive-vertex ear F(K) and c_tr(K) satisfy the exact elementary identity c_tr=3-4F throughout the target class. The earlier all-convex-n-gon theorem already supplies optimal F and precisely the affine-regular equality class; translating it into c_tr and substituting the regular-hexagon value is routine and not a new motivated boundary, classification or structural lemma. No new nonsymmetric bound, quantitative stability or additional mathematical invariant is established. Correctness of the determinant proof does not by itself supply value.
